![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14199341/assets/f7a556f986c44b922908b79e3982e098eb7250d9d470092ba2c45bbffe190913.png)

Which of the following represents the shaded region above as a type II region in two-dimensional space?
question.worked_solution:
A type II region can be written as

$$
D=\{(x,y)\,:\,a\le y\le b,\,g(y)\le x\le f(y)\},
$$

where $f$ and $g$ are continuous functions.

To express the given region as a type II region, we first rewrite all of the given curves as functions of $y:$

$$
y=2x\,⟹\,x=\frac{y}{2}
$$

The function $x=\sqrt{y}+1$ is already written as a function of $y.$

Notice that the region lies between the horizontal lines $y=1$ and $y=4.$ So, we have $1\le y\le 4.$

We draw a horizontal arrow through the region to determine the left function $g(y)$ and the right function $f(y).$ A horizontal line should intersect the region in a single interval only for it to be a type II region.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14199341/assets/c55d5f809462b767122ccc4af97c5b4d243730ed24f655bdc18e35ec57e25ce2.png)

The horizontal line enters the region through the lower function $x=\frac{y}{2}$ and leaves through the upper function $x=\sqrt{y}+1.$ So, we have $\frac{y}{2}\le x\le \sqrt{y}+1.$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
D=\{(x,y)\,:\,1\le y\le 4,\,\frac{y}{2}\le x\le \sqrt{y}+1\}.
$$
